0D76.name: Mario tile DMA source
desc: First entry of a table of 16-bit source addresses for the per-frame Mario graphics DMA. The routine at
$00:A3DF reads it as the source of a $80 or $40 byte VRAM copy ($0D78, $0D7A ... $0D80 are the next entries).
Written by the animated tile routine in bank $05 (STA $0D76,X, X counting down by 2).

0D82.name: Mario palette pointer
desc: Address (in bank $00) of the 20-byte ($14) palette that MarioGFXDMA copies to CG-RAM colour $86 each frame.
Set by the Mario draw routine (from DATA_00E2A2 indexed by Y, picks the colour set for the power-up/pose);
also read by the finish-pose code at $00:B04E.

0D84.name: Mario GFX DMA list size
desc: Size of the Mario graphics DMA list: how many tile pieces MarioGFXDMA copies this frame. 0 = skip the palette
transfer. The routine repeats the last segment while X < [$0D84].
Set to $0A by the controller-clear/Mario GFX setup code, to 6 in the overworld border icon drawing (probably),
and cleared by the enemy parade cutscene (game mode 25).

0D8B.name: Dynamic gfx source, top, slot 3
0D8B.kind: word (little endian), entry of the $0D85 table
desc: Source address of the top row of tiles for a dynamically drawn sprite graphic, copied to VRAM by the Mario/
dynamic graphics DMA (it is entry +6 of the table starting at $0D85, read at $00:A355).
Written by the flame/Podoboo draw ($8500 + offset), Yoshi head/wings draw and the Pipe Lakitu / Baby Yoshi
helpers. Its partner for the bottom row is $0D95 (= $0D8B + $0200).

0D95.name: Dynamic gfx source, bottom, slot 3
0D95.kind: word (little endian), entry of the $0D8F table
desc: Source address of the bottom row of tiles for a dynamically drawn sprite graphic (entry +6 of the table
starting at $0D8F, read at $00:A375). Always set to the top-row address in $0D8B plus $0200, 16 tiles later.
Written by the same routines as $0D8B: flames/Podoboo, Yoshi, Pipe Lakitu and Baby Yoshi.

0D9B.name: Special level mode
desc: Selects the special screen mode of the current level or screen. Normal levels use 0. The NMI and IRQ handlers
test it to pick the normal path or the Mode 7 / battle path, and sprite code uses it to adapt to Mode 7 rooms.
Loaded per level from SpecialLevTable ($05:85xx); set to 1 by title/credits-style game modes and to 2 by
game mode 0C setup. Read heavily by the NMI, status bar, Mode 7 boss sprites and OAM routines.
Bit 7: Mode 7 / battle style screen (BPL tests in NMI and IRQ).
Bit 6: Mode 7 boss room (tested with BIT, V flag); $C1 is the value checked for boss rooms.
Values: 0 = normal level, 1 and 2 = special mini-modes used by cutscene/overworld code.

0D9F.name: HDMA enable mirror
desc: RAM mirror of $420C. The NMI handler copies it to the HDMA channel enable register every frame, so setting a
bit turns that HDMA channel on from the next frame. Many routines write 0 to disable all HDMA (title screen,
message box, level end); the window effect setup writes $80 to enable channel 7 only.
Values: 0 = no HDMA. Bit n = channel n enabled.

0DA2.name: Joypad 1 held, high byte
desc: Joypad 1 buttons currently held, high byte of $4218, stored each frame by the controller read routine.
Bits: 7 B, 6 Y, 5 Select, 4 Start, 3 Up, 2 Down, 1 Left, 0 Right.
Indexed by player ([$0DA2,X]) when the controller routine picks which pad feeds Mario ($0DA0 or $0DB3).

0DA3.name: Joypad 2 held, high byte
desc: Joypad 2 buttons currently held, high byte of $421A/$421B read. Same bit layout as $0DA2 (B Y Select Start
D-pad). Written by the controller read routine; also tested in game mode 14 (in level) for player 2 input.
Bits: 7 B, 6 Y, 5 Select, 4 Start, 3 Up, 2 Down, 1 Left, 0 Right.

0DA4.name: Joypad 1 held, A/X/L/R
desc: Joypad 1 buttons currently held, low byte of $4218 masked with $F0. Written by the controller read routine,
then merged into $15/$17 (Mario's controller bytes). Hits from $0D:A4xx are table bytes, not real reads.
Bits: 7 A, 6 X, 5 L, 4 R.

0DA5.name: Joypad 2 held, A/X/L/R
desc: Joypad 2 buttons currently held, low byte masked with $F0. Written once per frame by the controller read
routine. Almost all the other listed uses are pointer table bytes in bank $0D, not accesses to this byte.
Bits: 7 A, 6 X, 5 L, 4 R.

0DA6.name: Joypad 1 newly pressed, high byte
desc: Buttons of joypad 1 (high byte) that went down this frame: (old EOR new) AND new. Used by menus, the lives
exchange and the overworld, which read it via [$0DA6,X] for the current player. Hits in bank $0D are table bytes.
Bits: 7 B, 6 Y, 5 Select, 4 Start, 3 Up, 2 Down, 1 Left, 0 Right.

0DA7.name: Joypad 2 newly pressed, high byte
desc: Buttons of joypad 2 (high byte) newly pressed this frame, computed in the controller read routine. The lives
exchange tests Start on either pad by ORing this with $0DA6. Bits as $0DA6.

0DA8.name: Joypad 1 newly pressed, A/X/L/R
desc: Joypad 1 A/X/L/R buttons newly pressed this frame ((old EOR new) AND new). Read by overworld mode 0E and
similar code; the $0D:A2xx hits are pointer table bytes. The partner for joypad 2 is $0DA9.
Bits: 7 A, 6 X, 5 L, 4 R.

0DAA.name: Joypad 1 previous high byte
desc: Joypad 1 high byte as it was last frame. Written at the end of the controller routine (STY) and used next
frame to find newly pressed buttons for $0DA6. Hits from $0D:Axxx are table bytes.

0DAB.name: Joypad 2 previous high byte
desc: Joypad 2 high byte remembered from last frame, used next frame to compute the newly pressed bits in $0DA7.
Hits from $0D:Axxx and $0D:C1xx are pointer table bytes.

0DAC.name: Joypad 1 previous A/X/L/R
desc: Joypad 1 A/X/L/R held bits remembered from last frame, so the next frame can compute $0DA8.

0DAD.name: Joypad 2 previous A/X/L/R
desc: Joypad 2 A/X/L/R held bits remembered from last frame, so the next frame can compute $0DA9.

0DAE.name: Screen brightness mirror
desc: RAM mirror of the screen brightness register $2100. The NMI copies it to $2100 each frame. Fades add to or
subtract from it; game modes set it to 0 (black) at start and $0F when showing the screen.
Values: $00 = black, $0F = full brightness (bit 7 would force blank).

0DAF.name: Mosaic fade direction
desc: Direction of the mosaic fade used by game modes 0F/13 and the overworld level name code.
Set to 1 when the screen is loaded for Nintendo Presents, cleared when Mario Start begins, XORed with 1
when the fade finishes so the next fade runs the other way. Used as an index into the fade step tables.
Values: 0 = fade in, 1 = fade out (probably, as seen from the level name code).

0DB0.name: Mosaic size
desc: Mosaic size for the fade effect, high nibble. Combined as $03 | [$0DB0] and written to $2106 so BG1 and BG2
are mosaicked. Starts at $F0 when a fade begins and steps by $10 per frame; 0 = no mosaic.

0DB1.name: Fade delay counter
desc: Frame countdown shared by the fade routines. KeepModeActive sets it to 1, other code sets it to 2 or 8;
the fade code decrements it each frame and acts when it goes negative, so the fade runs a step every
few frames. Also used the same way by the overworld level name text and the overworld save code.

0DB2.name: Two player game flag
desc: Number of players minus 1, set on the player select screen. 0 = one player (Mario only), 1 = two players
(Mario and Luigi). Read by the overworld and lives code to decide whether to swap players.
Values: 0 = 1 player, 1 = 2 players.

0DB3.name: Current player
desc: Which player is currently playing. Used as an index into the per-player tables from $0DB4 up (lives, coins,
power-up, Yoshi color, item) and times 3 as the score offset. Flipped with EOR #$01 when the players swap.
Values: 0 = Mario, 1 = Luigi.

0DB4.name: Player lives
0DB4.kind: byte table, one per player (index X)
desc: Lives of each player, stored as lives minus 1, so 0 means one life left and $FF (negative) means none left.
$0DB4 is Mario, $0DB5 is Luigi. A new game sets both to 4 (5 lives shown). Saved from the status bar on
overworld load, loaded back at Mario Start; the lives exchange screen reads and swaps them.

0DB5.name: Luigi lives
desc: Luigi's lives, the second entry of the [$0DB4,X] table (also stored as lives minus 1).
A new game writes $FF here for a one-player game; the Mario Start code ORs both players' lives to detect
a double game over. The lives exchange compares it with Mario's lives. $0D:A2xx hits are table bytes.

0DB6.name: Player coins
0DB6.kind: byte table, one per player (index X)
desc: Each player's coin count (word access at start clears both). $0DB6 is Mario, $0DB7 is Luigi.
Saved from the status bar coins ($0DBF) when the overworld loads and copied back when a level is entered.

0DB8.name: Player power-up
0DB8.kind: byte table, one per player (index X)
desc: Each player's saved power-up state ($0DB8 Mario, $0DB9 Luigi). Cleared to 0 (small) at new game, stored
from $0019 when the overworld loads and restored when a level is entered.
Values: 0 = small, 1 = big, 2 = cape, 3 = fire.

0DBA.name: Player Yoshi color
0DBA.kind: byte table, one per player (index X)
desc: Yoshi color each player carries, 0 = no Yoshi. $0DBA is Mario, $0DBB Luigi. Saved on overworld load,
copied into $0DC1, $13C7 and $187A when a level starts. Also used to pick the Yoshi map sprite color.

0DBC.name: Player reserve item
0DBC.kind: byte table, one per player (index X)
desc: Reserve (item box) item of each player ($0DBC Mario, $0DBD Luigi). Saved when the overworld loads, and
copied to $0DC2 on entering a level or switching players.

0DBE.name: Status bar lives
desc: Lives of the current player as shown on the status bar, stored as lives minus 1 (display adds 1).
Clamped to $62 (99 shown), decremented when Mario dies, set to 4 for a new game. Copied to and from
[$0DB4,X] when the player or screen changes. Negative means game over.

0DBF.name: Status bar coins
desc: Coin counter of the current player. Incremented per coin by the status bar update; cleared on new game.
Saved to [$0DB6,X] on overworld load and loaded back from it when a player's level or turn starts.

0DC0.name: Coins to collect
desc: Down counter, set to $1E (30) at level start when [$141A] is 0. The coin counter in bank $05 subtracts
coins collected from it, flooring at 0. Block code tests it for the special ? block: if it is 0 a different
sprite is spawned. Purpose beyond that is unclear; probably coins left before a reward.

0DC1.name: Overworld Yoshi color
desc: Yoshi color for the player on the overworld, 0 = no Yoshi. Copied from [$0DBA,X] when a level starts,
set by the level-end coin and Yoshi routines when Yoshi stays with Mario, and cleared on death/new game.
Values: 0 = no Yoshi, nonzero = Yoshi color.
